subject: Workspace bootstrap & service-token orchestration for BridgeLabs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Jefferson <ava@bridgelabs.com>, Sam Patel <sam@bridgelabs.com>
Cc: onboarding@bridgelabs.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Workspace bootstrap & service-token orchestration for BridgeLabs

Hi Ava / Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I drafted a short bootstrap plan so we can get your org usable within the next 72 hours without blocking your SRE team. Key goals: create the initial project namespaces, seed a small number of service tokens for integration testing, and invite the first set of admins.

Please confirm the following so we can start:
- The two admin users for initial invites (name + email).
- Whether you want SSO (SAML) enforced immediately or after token seeding.
- Any compliance constraints on token TTL / rotation cadence.

Proposed minimal plan (we can iterate):
1) Create projects: bridge-production, bridge-staging (isolated quotas).
2) Seed 3 short-lived service tokens (30d TTL) scoped to project-level write + read; one long-lived read-only token for monitoring (rotation encouraged).
3) Invite two admins into org with "Org Admin" role and seed one "Integration" user for CI.
4) Share an invite CSV and a seed report once done.

Attached: BL-MAP1.xlsx — mutual action plan with timelines.

If that looks good, reply with the admin emails and preferred SSO timing and Monica (cc'd on next email) will orchestrate the seed.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Ava Jefferson <ava@bridgelabs.com>

Cc: Sam Patel <sam@bridgelabs.com>, onboarding@bridgelabs.com
Date: 2026-10-25T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Workspace bootstrap & service-token orchestration for BridgeLabs

Thanks Jonas — this looks good. Quick answers:

- Admins for initial invites:
  - Sam Patel <sam@bridgelabs.com> (Engineering Manager)
  - Ava Jefferson <ava@bridgelabs.com> (Head of Integrations)
- We'd like SSO enforced after the initial seed (so our CI integrations can validate tokens first).
- Compliance: tokens used for production workloads must rotate every 30 days; monitoring/read-only may be 90 days. No HSM requirement for the initial rollout.

A couple of questions from our side:
- Can Redwood support per-project token scopes that exclude access to customer PII? We want monitoring tokens to be read-only and never return PII.
- Do you have a recommended naming convention for tokens so we can track them in our secret manager?

I attached the admin CSV with preferred display names. We'll also request SSO metadata from our IdP; I'll drop that into the Drive link once available.

Best,
Ava
Ava Jefferson
Head of Integrations | BridgeLabs
ava@bridgelabs.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Workspace bootstrap & service-token orchestration for BridgeLabs — seed request

Monica / Aditya / Ben — forwarding BridgeLabs' confirmations and asks. TL;DR: seed two org admins, create bridge-production & bridge-staging projects, seed 3 service tokens (2 x 30d, 1 x 90d read-only), enforce SSO after seed. Compliance wants 30d rotation for production tokens.

Please run the following checklist and reply with the seed-report and invite CSV when done:
- [ ] Create projects: bridge-production, bridge-staging.
- [ ] Create roles: org-admin (full), project-dev (read/write for project), project-ro (read-only for monitoring).
- [ ] Seed tokens with names following pattern: brg-<env>-<purpose>-<shortid> (e.g. brg-prod-ing-01). Put TTL on tokens per compliance notes.
- [ ] Create initial user invites for Sam / Ava as Org Admins and one integration user: bridge-ci@bridgelabs.com (we'll seed one integration token tied to that user).
- [ ] Generate seed-report.txt with token fingerprints (last 4 chars only), project ids and invite ids. Do not transmit token secrets in email; use Drive or the secure channel.

Notes: BridgeLabs asked that monitoring tokens never surface PII — ensure scope excludes user_data/read endpoints. If this is not possible with the current model, propose a code path to redact PII at the API layer and document it in the report.

Target: complete initial seed within 24-48 hours.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas — quick status update. Completed the checklist below and uploaded the deliverables to the Drive folder linked in related_links. Summary:

What I completed:
- Projects created: bridge-production (proj_8172), bridge-staging (proj_8173).
- Roles created: org-admin, project-dev, project-ro.
- Service tokens seeded (no secrets in email):
  - brg-prod-ing-01 (30d TTL) — integration token for CI
  - brg-prod-ro-01 (90d TTL) — monitoring read-only
  - brg-stg-ing-01 (30d TTL) — staging integration
- Invites sent to: Sam Patel (org-admin), Ava Jefferson (org-admin), bridge-ci@bridgelabs.com (integration user).

Attachments uploaded to Drive and also attached here for audit: seed-report-bridge.txt (contains token fingerprints, project ids, invite ids) and invites-bridge.csv (invite id + email + role).

Notes on PII and monitoring tokens: the runtime supports field-level redaction via policy. I enabled a monitoring-only scope that rejects endpoints which return user PII — validated with a quick test against the staging index. Documented in the seed-report.

Next steps:
- Jonas: confirm whether BridgeLabs wants us to enable SSO enforcement tomorrow (we can switch without rotating short-lived tokens).
- Aditya: please add a quick secret-policy note to the onboarding playbook recommending the naming convention and rotation automation (I used brg-<env>-<purpose>-<shortid>).

--
Monica Patel
